help.title:
Bring the films you love
closer to you.
help.intro: Connect your Jellyfin library or open shared videos on a computer or NAS. Start here, from your first connection to a comfortable way to watch.
help.jellyfin_note: Explore your library, actors and favorites. Pick up where you left off.
help.smb_note: Play compatible videos already exported to your computer or NAS.
help.scope: Ensceno is a player. It does not provide a film library or video subscription. Use media you are entitled to access and play. This guide covers the features in version 0.6.0.

sections.title: Open Ensceno for the first time
sections.html:
You need an Apple Vision Pro and either an existing Jellyfin server or a computer / NAS with SMB file sharing enabled. Allow local network access when connecting to a local device for the first time.

No server ready yet? Choose Play a sample. The synthetic video included with the app needs no account or network connection. Try playback in a window, system full screen or your private cinema.

You can switch between Chinese and English during setup. Media titles, actor names and other information come from your sources; changing the interface language does not automatically translate them.

sections.title: Connect Jellyfin
sections.html:
1. Choose Jellyfin during setup, or add a Jellyfin connection in Sources.
  2. Enter your server address, including http:// or https://, its port and any path your server uses. Get the address from your own setup or your server administrator.
  3. Sign in with your account on that Jellyfin server. You can also use Quick Connect when your server allows it.
  4. Select the libraries you want to show, let the content load, then open a video to play it.

At home, Vision Pro and your local server must be on networks that can reach each other. Away from home, your administrator needs to provide a working remote address. Ensceno does not provide a remote relay service.

If the same server address does not open in a browser, check the server, network and account first. If it works in the browser but not in Ensceno, note the error message and check local network permission.

sections.title: Connect a shared folder on a computer or NAS
sections.html:
1. Enable SMB file sharing on your computer / NAS and give your account read access to the video folder.
  2. Connect Vision Pro to the same reachable network. In Ensceno, open Sources → Add SMB share.
  3. Enter the Address, Shared folder name, Username and Password. The share name is the name published by your NAS, such as Videos, not a full disk path.
  4. You can use Find shared folders to choose a share. Select Connect and choose a folder, then choose the folder containing your videos.
  5. Select Save and scan. Open a video from your library after the scan.

Leave Domain empty unless your server requires it. SMB access is currently read-only. It does not offer server transcoding or remote deletion of shared files.

Start with compatible videos exported as MP4, MOV or M4V. The same extension can contain different video codecs, audio tracks and resolutions, so not every file is guaranteed to play.

Insta360 footage: stitch and export it on your computer first, preserving the intended projection and stereo layout. Original .insv footage cannot be played as if it were an exported video.

sections.title: Choose a playback mode
sections.html:
The Jellyfin player's Playback mode control lets you switch manually. Start with Automatic and adjust if needed:

ModeWhen to use it
AutomaticTries direct play first, then remuxing or transcoding if needed.
Direct playPlays the original file. Your device must support its codec and your network must carry its bitrate.
Original qualityKeeps the video encoding while changing its container / delivery format. Audio or subtitles may be processed. Requires a route supplied by your server.
CompatibleAsks Jellyfin to re-encode the video. This may reduce quality and requires more server processing.

Transcoding happens on your Jellyfin server. HLS does not always mean the video has been re-encoded: a remuxed stream can also use HLS. Check the current route shown in the player.

If a requested route is unavailable, the app displays a message and keeps the current playback. Apple spatial video requires direct playback to preserve its stereo information. SMB uses direct play and cannot switch to server transcoding in the app.

sections.title: Adjust the picture and viewing position
sections.html:
Choose 2D, VR180 or VR360 to match the video, then check side-by-side / top-bottom layout and eye order. If the picture is doubled, stretched or uncomfortable, use Fix picture to correct the format.

If videos in a library share the same format, open Default video format in that library's menu, for example VR180 with side-by-side stereo. An individual video's manual setting takes priority. Clear its individual format setting to follow the library default again.

Use Recenter to place the picture in your current viewing direction. Move the control window using the system bar beneath it. With hand tracking allowed, pinch your thumb and middle finger to hide or show controls.

Watch 2D video in a window, system full screen or your private cinema. The private cinema uses a minimal dark environment with adjustable screen size, distance, curvature and viewing posture. Start with small, comfortable adjustments.

sections.title: Actors, favorites and resume playback
sections.html:
Actors: open a person from a video's details or the Actors sidebar tab. You can see information supplied by your server and related works in your library. If actors are missing, check their metadata in Jellyfin first. SMB does not automatically create a Jellyfin actor directory.

Favorites: videos and actors use consistent favorite controls. Jellyfin favorites sync to the current account on the corresponding server. Favorites lets you browse videos and actors separately. Each source and account keeps its own favorites.

Watch later and lists: use these to organize videos on this device. They do not currently sync as Jellyfin playlists across devices.

Resume: Jellyfin receives playback status and progress; SMB resume positions are stored on your device. Leaving playback returns you to the previous browsing page and position. The position may change if content has been removed.

sections.title: Remove a source or delete a video
sections.html:
Remove a local source: removing a connection in Sources clears that source's local credentials, index and related information. It does not delete the account or media on your server.

Delete original files: this is a separate operation in a Jellyfin video's More menu. Deletion requires the necessary permissions and other checks. Stop playback from that server first and carefully review the server, file paths and scope shown in the confirmation.

Jellyfin may also delete parts, other versions, subtitles and artwork in the video's directory, affecting other devices. Ensceno cannot undo deletion or guarantee that files go to a trash folder. If the connection is interrupted, refresh the library and check the result on the server.

SMB does not offer original-file deletion. To clear local information, remove all saved sources before uninstalling the app, so Keychain credentials that might otherwise survive uninstalling can be removed.

faqs.q: I can see the file, but the picture is black or only audio plays.
faqs.a: Being able to read a file does not mean the current playback route can decode its video. For Jellyfin, try Original quality first, then Compatible if needed. SMB has no server transcoding; export a compatible video on your computer or play it through Jellyfin. Use the offline sample to check basic playback first.

faqs.q: A transcoded video plays for a few seconds, then stalls.
faqs.a: Check the route and transcoding speed in your Jellyfin dashboard. If conversion cannot keep up with playback, buffering will repeat. Try a remux that preserves the video, check hardware acceleration on your server, or prepare a compatible export. High-bitrate direct play and remuxing still need enough network bandwidth.

faqs.q: What should I check if SMB times out?
faqs.a: Check whether the host address changed, SMB is enabled, the account can read the share and Ensceno has local network permission. Guest Wi-Fi, device isolation and VPN / proxy rules can also block local access. You do not need to expose SMB ports to the internet for local playback.

faqs.q: Subtitles are missing or appear as squares.
faqs.a: Check that the right subtitle track is selected. If Jellyfin is burning subtitles into the video, the server or container needs fonts for that language. A browser and Ensceno may use different subtitle routes, so working browser subtitles do not rule out missing server fonts. Include the subtitle format and current playback route in your report.

faqs.q: Actor pictures, biographies or video information are missing.
faqs.a: Ensceno mainly displays information supplied by your chosen source. Add or correct actor and video metadata in Jellyfin, then refresh the library. This version does not initiate online TMDB matching; SMB folders do not automatically have a complete actor and film database.

faqs.q: Where can I send beta feedback?
faqs.a: TestFlight testers can open Apple's TestFlight, select Ensceno and choose Send Beta Feedback. You can also use the support email below. Explain whether sound and playback progress continue when the problem occurs. Do not send passwords or private media.

privacy.title:
Your library.
In your hands.
privacy.intro: This policy explains how Ensceno handles information on your device, when it communicates with your chosen server and how you can manage your data.
privacy.summary: This version has no ads, cross-app tracking or developer-operated behavioral analytics. Playback still communicates with your selected media services. When you send feedback, the developer receives the information you submit.

sections.title: 1. Scope and responsibility
sections.html: This policy applies to Ensceno (入境) version 0.6.0 and its support website, provided by SHENGJIE SUN. Ensceno is an independent media player for Apple Vision Pro. It does not operate your Jellyfin or SMB server or provide a film library. Public contact information is at the end of this page.

sections.title: 2. Connections and authentication
sections.html:
When you add a source, the app sends the information required for sign-in and file access to the Jellyfin or SMB service you specify, to authenticate, read your library and play content. Jellyfin requests also include the app name and version, client device name and an identifier generated on your device, so the server can identify the client and playback session.

The app does not store your Jellyfin sign-in password. Jellyfin access tokens and SMB passwords used to reconnect are stored separately for each source in your device's Keychain, with protection limited to that device. Source addresses, account names and selected folders are stored locally. These connections do not automatically send your passwords or tokens to the developer.

Your server and network administrators may log connection IP addresses, accounts, file access and playback activity according to their settings. Connection security also depends on the address, protocol and server configuration you choose.

sections.title: 3. Information stored on your device
sections.html:
To display your library and resume playback, the app stores media indexes, file and resource identifiers, cached artwork, playback positions, manual metadata corrections, video formats and library presets, playback preferences and browsing state locally. Watch later and custom lists are also stored locally. Cache, system backup and device migration handling additionally depend on Apple's systems and your settings; Keychain credentials use device-only storage.

Your device reads SMB directories and plays their media directly. The app currently accesses SMB shares in read-only mode.

sections.title: 4. Jellyfin sync and media requests
sections.html:
During Jellyfin playback, the app sends start, progress, pause and stop information to the corresponding server for resume playback and session management. Favoriting or unfavoriting videos and actors also sends those actions to the current account for that source.

Media, subtitles, posters and person images load from your selected service and the resource addresses it supplies. If a resource address belongs to a third party, your device may request it directly; that party receives network information needed to deliver it, such as an IP address. This version does not enable online TMDB matching initiated by the app.

sections.title: 5. Local network and spatial interaction
sections.html:
Local network permission is used to access the local media services you specify. Hand and head tracking support live gestures, control interactions and video positioning. The app does not persist or upload raw tracking data such as hand joints or head poses to the developer. On-screen controls remain available if you deny hand tracking.

You can manage the app's local network and hand tracking permissions in visionOS Settings. Disabling them may affect local connections or gestures.

sections.title: 6. Local diagnostics and Apple testing services
sections.html:
The app keeps local playback diagnostics limited to 512 KiB to help investigate route selection, buffering, placement status and errors. Release builds record only selected events and fields, such as internal media identifiers, playback time, bitrate, error codes and app version. They do not record passwords, tokens, server URLs or media titles, and are not automatically uploaded to the developer. Older diagnostics are replaced when the size limit is reached.

Feedback and screenshots you submit through TestFlight, and crash or test diagnostics Apple provides under its service and your settings, may be available to the developer. They are governed by Apple's testing and privacy rules. See TestFlight and Apple's privacy policy.

sections.title: 7. Support information you send
sections.html:
When you email support, the developer receives your sender address, message and any screenshots or files you choose to attach. This information is used to reply, investigate problems, handle privacy requests and follow up on related matters, not for advertising profiles. Microsoft Outlook provides the email service, subject to the Microsoft Privacy Statement.

Send only information needed to investigate the issue. Remove passwords, access tokens, private server addresses and private media. Support records are retained only as needed to handle requests, follow up on related issues or meet necessary obligations, and are then deleted or anonymized. You can use the support email to request access, correction or deletion.

sections.title: 8. Support website
sections.html:
This website is hosted on GitHub Pages. Its code does not set advertising or analytics cookies, use visitor analytics scripts, embed third-party fonts, videos or tracking pixels, or collect information through web forms. Chinese and English use separate pages without storing a language preference.

GitHub processes access logs, including visitors' IP addresses, for hosting and security purposes, under the GitHub Privacy Statement. External links lead to services with their own policies. Email links open your mail app; the developer receives an email only when you send it.

sections.title: 9. Management, retention and deletion
sections.html:
Source settings, indexes and viewing information support ongoing functionality and are generally retained until you remove the relevant information or app. The system may also clear caches. You can unfavorite items, edit lists and remove sources in the app. Signing out alone keeps the address and account name for your next sign-in.

Removing a source in Sources clears its local credentials, index and related information. It does not delete remote accounts, server favorites or media. To clear all local information, remove all saved sources before uninstalling the app, so Keychain credentials that might otherwise survive uninstalling can be removed. You or your server administrator manage records and accounts stored by those services.

The developer cannot access or delete content on your private server through this support website. For support information the developer actually holds, you can use the contact channel below to exercise applicable rights such as access, correction and deletion.

sections.title: 10. Deleting original files on a server
sections.html:
Delete original files in a Jellyfin video's details is a separate operation requiring explicit confirmation. The app checks permissions and shows the paths and scope returned by the server before sending a deletion request with the current account's credentials to the selected Jellyfin server. The server applies its own permissions and file rules.

Deletion may include parts, versions, subtitles and artwork in the same directory, and the app cannot undo it. File paths displayed in the confirmation are not written to playback diagnostics or automatically sent to the developer. SMB does not offer this feature.

sections.title: 11. Policy updates
sections.html: We update this page and its date when features or data handling change. Where new purposes or processing require authorization, we provide information and obtain the necessary authorization as applicable. The Chinese and English versions describe the same practices.

sections.html:
Ensceno uses AMSMB2 (MIT) and libsmb2 (GNU LGPL version 2.1 or, at your option, any later version) in the dynamically linked AMSMB2.framework. Their copyright notices and complete license texts accompany the app and the corresponding replacement materials.

SHENGJIE SUN permits recipients to modify their copy of Ensceno for their own use and to reverse engineer it for debugging those modifications, including modifications needed to replace the LGPL-covered library with an interface-compatible version. These permissions apply to the combined work, not only to the library. They prevail over conflicting restrictions in the license terms for Ensceno to the extent necessary to exercise these permissions. Third-party components retain their own licenses and rights.

For each externally distributed version, the corresponding materials include the exact library source and build instructions, an unencrypted application executable and required resources, and the replacement tool. Use those materials rather than attempting to decrypt an App Store download. A modified copy can be signed with your own development identity and provisioned for your device using Apple's developer tools. No Ensceno private signing key is provided or required.

This permission does not grant a general right to redistribute Ensceno's proprietary application binary, branding or private source code. It does not restrict redistribution or other rights granted by the licenses of the third-party components.

sections.title: Verification and next versions
sections.html:
A modified source copy was built for a visionOS device, retained all 833 original exports and passed replacement and local ad-hoc signature checks. The app machine-code section was unchanged. Actual execution of the modified library and one SMB browse/play check on Vision Pro remain pending. These engineering checks are not a legal opinion.

Use your own development signing identity and an independent bundle ID to install a modified copy. Keep your existing app and data. Each future externally distributed build requires matching materials; do not substitute build 33 materials for another build.
